title: Move a box to a sensor
summary: Start a belt from a button and stop it when a box reaches the sensor at the far end.
scope: Tests give deterministic native POSIX host evidence on a simulated plant scene; they are not physical, hardware, HIL, or certification evidence.
objectives: Start an actuator from a button press and remember that it is running.
Stop the actuator when a sensor sees the box.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/BeltToSensor.st, keep a Running memory: set it with Start, clear it with EyeFar, and wire Run and Emit.
stages.checkpoint: Run follows the memory; Emit puts one box on the belt when Start is pressed.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the box: the start button is only a short press, but the belt has to keep running until the box arrives.
stages.checkpoint: Belt off before the press; on after it, with one box on it; off again as soon as EyeFar sees the box, and it stays off.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then run: The starter drives no output, so the belt never moves; start the belt and put a box on it with Start, and stop the belt when EyeFar sees the box.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press Run (F5) and open the 3D view.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named belt-to-sensor and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the box ride the belt in the 3D view and stop under the sensor; compare it with the Run output in the trace.
stages.checkpoint: Run falls when the sensor turns on, not before, and the box is never dropped.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The EVENTUALLY assertion proves the sensor saw the box within eight seconds; the AT assertions pin the state at the start and at the end.
stages.checkpoint: It does not establish physical belt speed, sensor response, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.

hints.text: Start is a pulse, so the belt needs a memory: set Running when Start is TRUE and clear it when EyeFar is TRUE.
Write the clear after the set so EyeFar wins when both are TRUE, then Run := Running and Emit := Start.

faultCases: The starter drives no output, so the belt never moves; start the belt and put a box on it with Start, and stop the belt when EyeFar sees the box.
